Schema.Reason.InPlace: One ALTER TABLE. The rows are not touched.
Schema.Reason.ChangeColumnType: A type change rewrites every row, and a value that will not convert is replaced without a word. Studio rebuilds the table instead, so the conversion is a CAST you can see and the casualties are counted first.
Schema.Reason.AddPrimaryKey: The engine refuses to add a primary key to a table that already exists.
Schema.Reason.DropPrimaryKey: The engine refuses to drop a column that is part of the primary key.
Schema.Reason.ReorderColumns: The language has no way to move a column.
Schema.Reason.ReplaceViewBody: There is no ALTER VIEW in this language, so the view is dropped and created again.
Schema.Reason.ReplaceTriggerBody: There is no ALTER TRIGGER in this language, so the trigger is dropped and created again.
Schema.Cap.AddColumn.Why: ADD COLUMN, including UNIQUE, CHECK, REFERENCES, DEFAULT and computed columns
Schema.Cap.DropColumn.Why: DROP COLUMN. The foreign key on it goes with it - an index on it does NOT, so Studio drops that first
Schema.Cap.Rename: Rename a column or a table
Schema.Cap.DefaultOrNotNull.Why: ALTER COLUMN - the only two properties of a column this engine changes
Schema.Cap.Constraints: Add or drop UNIQUE, CHECK, FOREIGN KEY
Schema.Cap.Constraints.Why: ADD CONSTRAINT / DROP CONSTRAINT, and the constraint must be named
Schema.Cap.ColumnType.Why: ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE rewrites the rows, and stops at the first value it cannot read - with nothing changed, and nothing said about the rest. A rebuild converts with a CAST the user can see, after counting every value that will not survive it
Schema.Cap.AddPrimaryKey.Why: The engine refuses: 'Adding PRIMARY KEY constraint to existing table is not supported'
Schema.Cap.ChangePrimaryKey: Remove or change a primary key
Schema.Cap.ChangePrimaryKey.Why: Dropping a key column is refused too: 'it is part of the primary key'
Schema.Cap.ColumnOrder: Change the order of the columns
Schema.Cap.ColumnOrder.Why: There is no syntax for it: FIRST, AFTER, MODIFY and CHANGE are all parse errors
Schema.Cap.ViewBody.Why: There is no ALTER VIEW and no CREATE OR REPLACE
Schema.Cap.TriggerBody.Why: There is no ALTER TRIGGER - and none to enable or disable one either
Schema.Absent.Reindex: Rebuilding an index in place - there is no REINDEX and no ALTER INDEX; Studio drops and creates it
Schema.Absent.EnableTrigger: Enabling or disabling a trigger - there is no ALTER TRIGGER
Schema.Absent.MoveColumn: Moving a column - there is no FIRST, AFTER, MODIFY or CHANGE
Schema.Absent.Sequence: A sequence's step, minimum, maximum or cycle - CREATE SEQUENCE takes a name and START WITH, nothing else

Structure.Key.AutoIncrement: The key is AUTOINCREMENT, so an insert does not scan for uniqueness and needs no index of its own.
Structure.Key.Indexed: The key has an index of its own, so an insert finds a duplicate without scanning.
Structure.Key.ManualNoIndex: The primary key is set by hand and has no index: every insert scans the whole table to check it. Adding a UNIQUE index on {0} removes that.
Grid.ReadOnly.NoKey: "{0}" has no primary key, so a row cannot be identified. The data is shown for viewing; edit it with a query that names the rows you mean.
Grid.Paging.NoKey: This table has no single-column primary key, so pages are counted from the start of the table: the further in you go, the longer it takes.
Grid.Conflict.RowGone: The row was changed or removed by another connection after it was read here.
Grid.Conflict.RowCount: The statement matched {0} where exactly {1} was expected.

Format.Reason.DoesNotParse: a statement that does not parse on its own stays as written
Format.Reason.CannotBeSerialized: the parser cannot write this kind of statement back out, so it stays as written

Database.Config.Source: from what the database recorded when it was created
Database.Now.NoTransaction: none - every statement commits on its own
Database.Now.HeldHere: held by this connection - no other application can open it while Studio has it
Database.Now.Busy: the path is locked, and the holder cannot be named: the operating system does not say
Database.Now.NotLocked: file locking is off for this connection, so another engine can open the same database
Database.Lsm.NoLevels: one flat set of files, merged into one - this store has no levels

Database.Lsm.Compact.Name: Merge the SSTables into one
Database.Maintenance.NotSupported: {0}: this store does not have it
Database.Cap.Dump: Dump of the schema and the data
Database.Cap.CacheOccupancy: How full the page cache is
Database.Cap.Source.Detector: the header, or provider.meta for LSM
Database.Cap.Source.FileCopy: copying the file or the folder
Database.Cap.Source.None: nothing - the key is derived when the database is created
Database.Cap.Note.CopyNeedsQuiet: nothing can pause the writes; a paged database is closed for the duration
Database.Cap.Note.LsmOnly: only an LSM store has files to merge
Database.Cap.Note.NoLevels: a count and a threshold - this store has no levels
Database.Cap.Note.PagedOnly: a paged database only - an LSM one has no page cache
Database.Cap.Note.NothingCounts: neither page cache counts a hit or a miss, so there is no rate to read
Database.Cap.Note.ReadCheckInstead: verification by reading is what Studio can do instead
Database.Cap.Note.MigrationInstead: a new database and a migration into it
Database.Cap.Source.Rewrap: the preamble - the password wraps the key, it does not derive it
Database.Cap.Note.RewrapNotMigration: replacing a password rewrites 60 bytes and no page; encrypting a database, or removing encryption, is still a migration
Database.Config.Unavailable: This database was created by the connection that is open now, and an open database's header cannot be read - not even its store type. What it was created with will be readable the next time it is opened.
ReadCheck.Note.NoColumns: the catalogue does not say which columns it covers, so there was nothing to walk it with
ReadCheck.Note.PlannerDidNotUseIt: the planner answered without it, so the index itself was not read - this engine will not consider an index below ten rows
ReadCheck.Note.NothingToSeekWith: the column holds no value to seek with, so the index was not reached
ReadCheck.Note.SeekNotTraversal: a seek and not a traversal: this engine reaches an index only through an equality, and answers ORDER BY and a range with a full scan
ReadCheck.Title: Verification by reading
ReadCheck.Heading: Verification by reading - {0}
ReadCheck.Open.Name: Read every table and every index and report what came back
ReadCheck.Rows.Name: What was read
ReadCheck.Stopped: Stopped after {0} objects - this is not a database that passed
ReadCheck.Disagreements: {0} tables whose counter disagrees with their rows
ReadCheck.Result.Inconclusive: {0}, but this proves nothing about the object itself
ReadCheck.Result.Disagrees: {0} read, and COUNT(*) says {1} - the counter and the rows disagree
ReadCheck.Limits: What this does NOT find: an inconsistent B-tree, lost pages, errors in the free lists. A real integrity check reads the structure; this reads the data through it, so a green run says nothing about the parts of the file nobody is using. It will exist when PRAGMA integrity_check does.
Copy.Title: Copy of the database
Copy.Heading: Copy of {0}
Copy.Open.Name: Take a byte copy of this database
Copy.NotADump: A copy of the bytes and not a dump: the encryption, the pages, the statistics and the format survive, so the copy opens instantly instead of having to be executed.
Copy.PartsNote: A database is more than its data file - the indexes live in a folder beside it and the journal in a file. All of it is taken; the lock sidecar is not.
Copy.Verify: Check the copy: open it and read its schema
Copy.WillClose: This is a paged database, and while the engine holds the file nothing can read it - not even byte by byte. The connection is closed for the duration of the copy and opened again afterwards. It comes back as a NEW connection: a tab that belonged to the old one keeps its text and does not adopt it.
Copy.TransactionOpen: A transaction is open on this connection. A copy taken now is of a database in the middle of a decision - the transaction is discarded when the connection closes.
Copy.NoRestore: There is no restore here. Putting a copy back means closing the connection, moving the file and opening it again; a restore button would promise a rollback inside a running application. What Studio does instead is open the copy as another connection, so the two can be compared.
Copy.Verified: the copy opens and names {0} tables
Copy.NotVerified: and the copy did NOT open: {0}
Copy.HeldOpen: The database is a paged file and something is holding it, so nothing can read the bytes.
Password.Step.Reading: The schema and the data are read out
Password.Step.Writing: They are written into the new database
Password.Step.Verifying: Every table is counted on both sides
Password.Title: Change the password
Password.Heading: Change the password of {0}
Password.Open.Name: Change the password by migrating into a new database
Password.Explanation: Encryption cannot be added to a database that has none, or taken away from one that has it, without rewriting every page. Studio builds a new database and carries the schema and the data across; the original is not touched.
Password.NoCurrent: The current password is not asked for: the database is open in front of you, so it has already been given and accepted. A field that is checked against nothing is theatre.
Password.SourceUntouched: The original is not changed. Delete it by hand once the new one has been checked.
Password.ConnectAfterwards: Connect to the new database when the transfer is done
Password.ItIsAScript: The transfer is a script that is executed again, not a copy of the bytes - so every table is counted on both sides afterwards, by reading the rows.
Password.Step.Rewrapped: the key was rewrapped under the new password; no page was rewritten
Password.RewrapDone: The password has been replaced. The database is the same file and this connection is still open.
Password.RewrapExplains: This database already has a password, so replacing it does not copy anything: the encryption key is wrapped by the password rather than derived from it, and only the wrapping is rewritten. The file, its pages and its indexes are untouched.
Password.RewrapWarning: The change is irreversible and no copy of the old password is kept anywhere. Nothing can open this database without the new one - keep it.
Password.RowsMatch: every table has the same number of rows on both sides
